doc.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

chapter: Manhattan School and the Benny Goodman Russian tour
title: Leaving Kai, Manhattan School of Music and the first New York jobs
summary: Sebesky urged him to study; Andre left the group in 1958, used his GI Bill at Manhattan School, and worked at CBS and with Mulligan.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: School of Music.” I don’t know if he said Manhattan, but that’s where he was going anyways. And he went back I think to school in September and left, and this trombone player, a very good trombone player from Cincinnati came on and took his place called Ola Hanson. And no he’s from Columbus. And it was while Ola was on the band that I left the group to settle in New York. It was in February of ’58. I came in for the second semester of school because I was on the verge. I’m a depression baby you know, so I was going to lose my GI bill if I didn’t get in school on time so I wasn’t going to lose that money. So I decided I’d better get in school you know. So I got in school and the government paid all my education at the Manhattan School of Music and I stayed there and I graduated in 1962 and that’s — I was around town and I was, I think I graduated, I’d taken some kind of exam and what knowledge I’d learned at Berklee helped me. I think I skipped a grade or something. I think I only went to Manhattan School and got a degree in about three years time. I think I went to summer school a bit too. And so then I was around town, I got the job at CBS, I was doing the Jackie Gleason Show and everything else. Then the next thing that comes was Gerry Mulligan’s concert jazz band. Then, not a turning point, but the big thing that happened is when I was asked to go to Russia with Benny Goodman’s band. 1962.
